comments.author: eminsk
comments.body:
I took a look at this and reproduced the crash with a test case.

When `max_width <= self.width + width_padding` (or with `width=0, padding=0`), `column_count` in `rich/columns.py` evaluates to `0`, causing the `ZeroDivisionError` when iterating.

Guarding `column_count` with `max(1, ...)` resolves the issue cleanly:
```python
column_count = (
    max(1, max_width // (self.width + width_padding))
    if (self.width + width_padding) > 0
    else 1
)
```

I've put together a fix with regression tests on my fork:
- Commit: [eminsk/rich@c9f68f3](https://github.com/eminsk/rich/commit/c9f68f339457092728cf5ac86264ad3d8571073c)
- Branch: [`fix/columns-zero-division`](https://github.com/eminsk/rich/tree/fix/columns-zero-division)

Since PRs are currently limited to collaborators on this repo, feel free to cherry-pick this directly or let me know if you'd like me to open a PR once permissions allow.

comments.author: TrueFurina
comments.body:
I hit this while using `Columns` with a fixed width and traced it to `rich/columns.py`. Here's a minimal fix — happy to send a proper PR if collaborators would like one (I can't open one due to the repository's collaborator-only pull request policy).

**Root cause:** in `__rich_console__`, when `self.width` is set:

```python
column_count = (max_width) // (self.width + width_padding)
```

If `self.width + width_padding > max_width` (e.g. `Columns(width=10)` on a console of width 10 with the default padding `(0, 1)`), this evaluates to `0`. `iter_renderables` then evaluates `item_count % column_count`, raising `ZeroDivisionError`.

**Fix:** clamp the column count to at least 1, falling back to a single column:

```python
column_count = max(1, max_width // (self.width + width_padding))
```

**Reproduction (rich 15.0.0):**

```python
from io import StringIO
from rich.console import Console
from rich.columns import Columns

console = Console(file=StringIO(), width=10)
console.print(Columns(["a", "b", "c"], width=10))  # ZeroDivisionError
```

After the fix this renders the items stacked in a single column.

Full fix with a regression test (`test_width_narrower_than_console_does_not_crash`, covering `width == console_width`, `width == 0` on a wider console, and `column_first` with an oversized width) is on my fork, built on current `main`:

**https://github.com/TrueFurina/rich/compare/main...TrueFurina:fix/columns-zero-width-fallback**

(`rich/columns.py` +4/-1, `tests/test_columns.py` +11; `pytest tests/test_columns.py` — 2 passed.)

Feel free to cherry-pick or use it as a base if a collaborator picks this up.
